decisions.question: Stream identity representation: collision-safe reserved label, native non-label dimension, or staged combination? If native, define storage, query/aggregation, vector matching, duplicate-series, remote-read, /series, label APIs and legacy clients, plus missing/invalid Entity fallback.
decisions.resolution: Decided for the current phase. Every series generated from OTLP or native OTAP carries the ordinary reserved label __otel_resource__, whose value is the hash of the associated logical Resource identity. Use this label rather than a new hidden or native identity dimension. The label participates in stored series identity and is representable through existing duplicate detection, queries, aggregation, vector matching, /series, label APIs, remote read, HTTP and legacy clients. It is an identity carrier, not descriptive metadata enrichment; retaining it does not violate 'metadata ignored by default'. Hashes are lookup and candidate encodings, not substitutes for complete canonical Resource identity and complete-content comparisons. Without usable EntityRefs, use today's explicit compatibility identity: service.name, service.namespace and service.instance.id, preserving absent-versus-empty distinctions. This is a clearly labelled compatibility fallback, not a universal OTel Resource-identity claim. With EntityRefs, hash the authoritative structured identity: each Entity's type; exact typed ID key/value pairs; Entity grouping and set membership; raw Resource attributes not associated with an Entity, which remain identifying; and all required typed content, without stringification. Description-only attributes do not participate. A key that is an ID for one Entity remains identifying even if another Entity uses it only as a description key. Schema URL context is preserved separately and is not silently folded into an identifying attribute. Malformed EntityRefs and duplicate same-type EntityRefs cause atomic rejection of the affected batch or transaction: no fixed-triplet fallback and no samples, metadata/index prefix, WAL prefix or committed-work counters. Adding, removing or changing valid EntityRefs may intentionally change the Resource and series identity; do not reinterpret it as an ordinary descriptive content update.
decisions.limits: Scope metadata may still be retained and queried, but Scope identity does not distinguish otherwise identical streams in this phase. This is a current-phase limitation, not a claim of complete Scope-injective stream identity and not a universal rule that Scope can never matter. Metric properties and data-point attributes remain distinct logical stream dimensions under existing translation semantics.

decisions.question: Association cardinality and conflicts: one owner per series/kind/time or several legitimate owners? For contradictory same-time and late/multi-writer claims, reject the transaction or retain samples with an explicitly unresolved association, and what is the replay result?
decisions.resolution: Decided. For current Resource, Scope, Metric, Resource-schema and Scrape relations, allow at most one active owner for a series and metadata kind at a particular time. Multiple independent domains can coexist; competing owners within one domain must not become implicit multiple enrichments. Genuine future many-to-many relations require explicitly named relation semantics rather than implicit exceptions. Conflict matrix: same owner, same complete content and same effective time is an idempotent observation with no new version, extending observation bounds only when needed; same owner and effective time with different complete content rejects the whole transaction atomically; same series/kind/effective time with different owners rejects the whole transaction atomically; same owner/content at another point in its existing epoch extends observation bounds only with no version; different content at a new effective time inserts an ordered actual version whose predecessor ends exclusively at that time; a different owner at a new effective time inserts an ordered membership band whose predecessor ends exclusively at that time; input addressing discarded or truncated state is rejected or exposes explicit truncation, never inventing exact history or resurrecting discarded state. Rejection publishes no samples, metadata/index prefix, WAL prefix or committed counter, and previously committed state is unchanged. Do not commit samples while retaining an unresolved contradictory association; no quarantine or conflict subsystem is selected. Effective time, not arrival time, defines validity and temporal order. Observation of the content or owner already applicable at that time only extends observation bounds. Backfilled actual content or membership changes insert ordered history and affect only the resulting band. Backfilled content equal to an immediate successor may coalesce that redundant successor while preserving both observation histories. Observation bounds never move across an actual content or membership change point. A/B/A produces a new A epoch after B; it does not extend the first A epoch through B. Content histories and membership histories follow those rules independently. No exact historical answer may be claimed from discarded or ambiguous observations. Arrival time, map iteration, writer name, receiver and OTAP batch ID are never precedence rules. Validate against committed state before publication and publish accepted transactions atomically. The same initial state plus a fixed ordered committed log must reproduce exactly the same history, memberships, observation bounds, truncation and errors on replay. Unrelated commit orders are not required to be commutative or to produce an arbitrary identical winner. Rejected transactions are not committed-log entries. Committed replay must not manufacture versions, memberships, metadata-only blocks or additional bounds. Flush, compaction or snapshot restore plus replay must reproduce the same retained state. Transport acknowledgements do not imply exactly-once delivery. No distributed transaction or coordination requirement follows.
decisions.limits: Source/provenance is deliberately excluded from the generic one-owner answer and remains decision 5; this decision does not settle Source as single-valued or multi-valued. Decision 3 (unknown, clearing and expiry) and all other open decisions remain unanswered. No quarantine or unresolved-conflict-retention subsystem is selected.

decisions.question: Unknown, clearing and expiry: which producer/API operation clears content or ends membership, is there an explicit lease or expiry separate from observation, and what does each query return for absent, unknown, cleared, truncated and coalesced states?
decisions.resolution: Decided. Observation is not expiry. Preserve typed present/null, absent, explicitly cleared, unknown, truncated and coalesced states distinctly. Keep three axes independent rather than collapsing them into a single found boolean: content (which value or assertion applies at a time), association applicability (which owner applies to the series or domain at that time) and history coverage (what retained evidence remains available to answer). Value and knowledge states: present means an authoritative assertion supplies the complete typed value; null means a typed null was explicitly supplied and is present, not absent or unknown; absent means an authoritative complete content assertion does not contain the key; cleared means an explicit deletion or tombstone says a previously meaningful value or association no longer applies; unknown means there is no applicable trustworthy assertion, observation or retained history from which to answer; truncated means an answer might have existed but retained coverage is explicitly incomplete and is not a successful current-value lookup; coalesced means examples or ranges were deliberately merged under policy and exact intermediate changes are not claimed. Missing keys in partial Resource descriptions mean unknown for that source, not absent or cleared. Partial input leaves unknown fields unresolved. Only authoritative complete content or an explicit policy can assert omission as absence. Provably redundant equal-successor coalescing is lossless and must not be relabelled lossy coalescing or truncation. A version-count cap alone is not a complete memory bound or a semantic definition of these states. Explicit key clear and explicit association termination are separate operations, usable in metadata-only transactions, replayed deterministically and durable across lifecycle operations. Explicit key clear: the old value ends at the clear's inclusive EffectiveFrom and the preceding version is exclusive immediately before it; no current value is promoted or returned; historical content before the clear remains readable; reappearance creates a new version; clearing one key does not clear unrelated keys; clearing every Resource attribute does not itself remove Resource identity or its series associations; other members and metadata domains are unaffected; repeated equivalent clears are idempotent observations under decision 2. Explicit association termination is represented as an actual membership successor: the previous owner ends at the termination time exclusively; later queries report the series as unassociated using the selected explicit semantics; later reassociation creates a new band; owner content and other series members are unaffected; owner history is not deleted by one member's departure. Equal-time owner-versus-owner or owner-versus-termination disagreement remains a decision-2 atomic conflict; the whole affected transaction rejects without publishing a prefix. Current metadata has no general wall-clock lease. No implicit expiry: do not infer expiry from ObservedFrom or ObservedUntil, missing observations or missed scrapes, sample staleness, process restart, close, replay, flush, compaction, rollout or wall-clock time, or arrival order or transport retry. Latest content remains applicable until an actual successor, explicit clear or policy-based retention. A disappearing series does not implicitly clear its Resource or Scope context. Close and reopen does not age metadata. No generic lease or TTL subsystem is selected for this phase; a future authoritative protocol expiry must be explicit domain-authorized validity state, not receiver timeout behavior or time.Now() construction. Queries expose absence and uncertainty rather than pretending these states are ordinary empty labels. Query behavior: existing queries and vector matching ignore metadata by default; unknown, absent, cleared and truncated states synthesize no fake promoted label; series lacking usable context survive unfiltered enrichment; positive value filters match only an applicable present value and absent, cleared or unknown do not silently equal an empty-string value; selecting a missing or cleared state requires an explicit state predicate rather than a magic value under an ordinary label matcher; range evaluation uses the applicable stable validity band and does not select one clear or reappearance arbitrarily for the entire range; one input series contributes at most once across clear, reappearance and association transitions; historical diffs express before/after state changes explicitly rather than encoding a clear as old->; reverse filtering still requires a common overlap of content validity, membership validity and query range; metadata-only clear, absence, truncation and history paths read zero sample payloads. No applicable association, an applicable owner with the key absent, a key explicitly cleared, and no exact answer because coverage is unknown or truncated must not all collapse to the same not-found response. Retention and coalescing change evidence coverage, not the meaning of retained facts: expose history truncation and, where representable, earliest retained coverage; preserve observation and association coverage limits; preserve a separate marker for lossy coalescing if introduced under policy; queries requiring discarded history report unknown or truncated, not absent or cleared; immutable older parts must not resurrect cleared values or associations; lossless equal-successor coalescing preserves combined observation ranges. Transactions and lifecycle: validate every change before publication; rejected clear or termination changes publish no samples, metadata/index prefix, WAL prefix or committed counter; metadata-only changes fabricate no samples or sample time coverage; replay and compaction preserve change order, tombstones, applicability, observation bounds and coverage flags exactly; arrival order cannot overwrite a newer committed value with an older one; close/reopen or newer immutable-part recovery cannot resurrect cleared state; partial multi-source descriptions preserve independent assertions and provenance and do not merge, clear or reconcile Resources from matching names alone.
decisions.limits: Decision 3 does not decide Source cardinality (decision 5), PR99 grammar (decision 6), typed HTTP or cursor schema (decision 7), coexistence (decision 8) or admission and retention budgets (decision 9). Exact PR99 syntax for selecting unknown, absent or cleared states and exact JSON/HTTP response encoding are deferred to decisions 6 and 7; this decision fixes only the semantic distinctions and query behavior they must preserve. No generic lease or TTL subsystem is selected for this phase. Current-phase limit: the incumbent has no typed-null, tombstone, association-termination, completeness/provenance or state-specific response representation; the accepted clear, termination, typed-state and partial-input clauses remain explicit non-passing target cases rather than being inferred from current prototype behavior.

decisions.question: Kubernetes acquisition and reconciliation: is collector-supplied per-series association sufficient or must plain scrape provide it? For partial container descriptions, is the target a combined view or a merged logical Resource, and which identifiers authorise it?
decisions.resolution: Decided. Collector-supplied association is sufficient for this phase. Authoritative collection pipelines may associate cAdvisor or other telemetry with pod, node and workload context before OTLP or OTAP export using authoritative Kubernetes watches and mappings, and Prometheus must preserve the supplied Resource identity, associations, temporal bounds, Entity grouping and provenance without rederiving them. For plain Prometheus scrape, target or discovery metadata may be stored as target or Scrape metadata, but target-level context must not be assigned arbitrarily to other objects the target exposes; no built-in per-series Pod->ReplicaSet->Deployment resolver is selected; _info, _owner, pod-name, ReplicaSet-name and workload-name patterns create no native association; without authoritative association results remain unknown or unassociated; and existing joins and recording rules remain the compatibility mechanism. Do not add a Kubernetes informer, Kubernetes API client or ownership graph to Prometheus, and do not require both collector and plain-scrape paths. A known component that drops EntityRefs is not assumed harmless: collection mapping must preserve them or add valid ones under an explicit producer or proxy policy before storage loses them. Authoritative object identity: names are descriptive, not authoritative identity. Use k8s.pod.uid for pod incarnation; pod UID plus container name for a named container; runtime container.id for a running execution, with restart count as descriptive context rather than a universal Entity ID; supplied UIDs plus applicable namespace, kind, cluster and source context for nodes and owning workloads; and old and new ReplicaSets as distinct objects that both map to the same authoritative Deployment during a rollout when collection supplies it. Collection must preserve logically distinct identities through valid typed EntityRefs or an explicit compatibility mapping such as a distinct service.instance.id or a deliberate UID-bearing label policy; a raw UID that is dropped or contributes to neither Resource nor series identity is insufficient. Missing authoritative identity produces an unresolved relationship, not a guessed merge; reusing pod, container, namespace or Deployment names does not conflate incarnations; deliberate name grouping in a query is a user choice rather than storage reconciliation. No general containment/relationship graph or Entity-event subsystem follows; Knowledge Graph is a use case and consumer, not a requirement to manufacture graph edges such as RUNS_ON in storage. Partial descriptions produce a combined context view, not a merged Resource: preserve original logical Resources and independent assertions, and group components only where authoritative typed Entity evidence establishes the relation, for example the same pod UID, the same pod UID plus named container, or a compatible runtime container.id for the same runtime execution. Every component retains its original Resource identity, complete typed content, Entity grouping and Schema URL context, producer/producer-source attribution, observation bounds and effective validity, and retained coverage or truncation state. No actual merger is selected: no merging of metric streams, no rewriting of stored Resource IDs, no universal replacement attribute map, no choosing manifest/runtime/image/owner values by newest observation, and no merging of Resources merely because names match. For the CronJob example, complementary manifest and runtime fields may be presented together only where authoritative identity establishes the relation; each value remains source-attributed; conflicting values retain their assertions and temporal and provenance context instead of selecting an arbitrary canonical winner; distinct restart and runtime executions remain distinct; insufficient UID or Entity evidence leaves Resources separate and the relation unresolved; and a field omitted from a partial description remains unknown for that source and cannot clear another source's assertion under decision 3. An actual OTel Resource merge, if a producer needs one, belongs outside Prometheus under OTel policy; no opportunistic merge algorithm is implemented in storage. Time, rollout, conflict and lifecycle: use supplied effective and validity evidence, and do not backdate context merely because an informer learned it later; without historical evidence applicability starts at the first supported observation; collection informer lag, collector restart, missed observations and the lack of another watch event do not implicitly clear or expire context; object disappearance needs explicit evidence before association termination, and no response is not proof of deletion; old and new rollout objects each contribute at most once and independently collected telemetry is not deduplicated as a side effect; contradictions within one authoritative Resource association follow decision 2's atomic rejection; different source assertions retained in a combined view remain independent rather than silently becoming one conflicting owner history; replay, flush, compaction, retention and close/reopen preserve identities, associations, provenance, observed and effective bounds, tombstones and coverage exactly; discarded history reports unknown or truncated under decision 3 rather than current absence; and no distributed transaction or coordination requirement follows. Use-case query outcomes: node filtering and grouping use authoritative supplied node context; workload filtering and grouping use resolved UID-aware ownership supplied at collection; series lacking context survive unfiltered aggregation and remain unattributed; no association duplicates an input series' contribution; historical evaluation uses applicable retained context at evaluation time; and combined views, discovery and navigation require no sample-payload reads. An unrestricted property graph, TraceQL, Entity-event ingestion or arbitrary resolution priority is not selected. Exact HTTP/JSON encoding and PromQL syntax remain decisions 6 and 7.
decisions.limits: Decision 4 does not decide Source cardinality (decision 5), PR99 grammar (decision 6), typed HTTP or cursor schema (decision 7), coexistence (decision 8), admission and retention budgets (decision 9) or representative performance targets (decision 10). Exact HTTP/JSON encoding and PromQL syntax remain decisions 6 and 7. No Kubernetes informer, Kubernetes API client, ownership graph, containment/relationship graph, Entity-event subsystem, unrestricted property graph or distributed transaction/coordination requirement is selected, and no actual OTel Resource merge is implemented in Prometheus. Current-phase limit: the incumbent has only the fixed service.* compatibility identity, ignores EntityRefs, keeps one untyped string content map per owner and has no combined-context view, per-source provenance, unresolved-relation state or authoritative UID identity; the accepted acquisition, identity and combined-view clauses remain explicit non-passing target cases rather than being inferred from prototype behaviour.

decisions.question: Source: final receiving transport, immediate sender, original producer, or complete observed provenance, and how are conflicting source claims represented?
decisions.resolution: Decided. Source is a typed provenance record of an ingestion observation, not a single source string and not the final transport. Roles are distinct: producer is the original telemetry producer, explicitly supplied and trusted; sender is the immediate upstream sender or collector, explicitly supplied and trusted; transport is the final-hop route actually used, a locally known fact. A receiver role is deliberately excluded from this phase because there is no accepted per-series requirement; if it is introduced later it is optional, local, configuration-only and never disambiguates producers. Transport never reports the original producer. Trust is fail-closed: only configured or authenticated actors populate producer or sender; untrusted, missing or dropped claims leave that role unknown; producer and sender are never inferred from Resource attributes, job or instance labels, hostnames, metric or target names, transport names, peer address, User-Agent, writer order, map iteration or OTAP batch IDs. No global producer registry is created. A proxy must not overwrite a known producer identity; it may assert a producer that is currently unknown only under an explicit trusted mapping or attestation policy, it must preserve the original observation, and it is represented as sender or hop rather than replacing the producer. Contradictory claims become explicit ambiguity where the accepted model permits them and never an arbitrary overwrite. Provenance is per observation or assertion, outside Resource content and stream identity. It never participates in __otel_resource__. Resource content must not churn merely because provenance changed. Provenance cannot repair a collapsed stream, split streams, merge Resources or authorise object reconciliation. Identical Resource content with different provenance leaves Resource identity and versions and sample contribution unchanged. Genuinely distinct logical streams must already be distinguished by Resource and series identity under decisions 1 and 4, and provenance cannot perform that separation afterwards. One active provenance-record association exists per series and validity time, compatible with decision 2's Source exclusion. One record contains a coverage scope, a completeness state and a canonical set of typed provenance components. A component carries exactly one transport, at most one sender and at most one producer. At most one producer component is normal; more than one requires the explicit ambiguity marker. Identical components deduplicate by candidate identity followed by complete canonical typed comparison, never digest-only trust, and equality is idempotence rather than additional multiplicity. Canonical sort order is representation only, never semantic precedence. Different components coexist only within a declared scope that permits both, such as several intermediate senders observing one logical stream. This is one record with multiple components, not a multi-owner Source relation, and no additional relation type is invented solely for the components. Producer and stream outcomes: distinct genuine logical producers or streams are distinguished by Resource and series identity and exposed as data. One logical stream observed through N senders keeps one Resource unless its content changed, carries N sender observations or components, and counts each input observation at most once. Redundant copies through different senders are sender observations, not evidence of different producers. Conflicting descriptive producer claims on an already collapsed or single stream may coexist only with the explicit unresolved or ambiguous marker; they are not authoritative exact producer attribution and cannot split, merge or reconcile afterwards. A missing trusted producer is always unknown. Same component identity and effective time with different complete content rejects atomically under decision 2 with no visible prefix. Complete and partial records: partial observations add evidence but cannot remove or clear an omitted component. Complete authoritative records replace the component set within their explicitly declared scope. Only a named trusted authority may declare completeness, for a specific coverage scope; if completeness is unprovable the record is partial, and 'all components observed' is not proof of global completeness. Component removal requires an explicit removal or clear marker with a valid time, and omission never removes. A merged partial state must carry its coverage scope and cannot masquerade as a complete current answer. Reappearance is a new version or membership band. Different content of the same component follows decision 2's atomic rejection. No map iteration, privilege order or identifier order selects an alternative answer. Temporal axes stay separate: metric sample time, supplied metadata validity or EffectiveFrom, actual observation or receipt coverage, commit publication, and replay or retention coverage. A historical sample timestamp alone cannot backdate producer, sender or transport validity or receipt; a sample timestamp is not the observation time of transport accepted now. Supplied authoritative metadata validity is used where supported. Actual receipt time may be observation coverage but never implicit validity or expiry, and it does not imply a generic wall-clock rule for other domains. No implicit expiry follows from observation bounds, missed input, restart, replay, flush, compaction, rollout, retry or wall clock; clear, termination and reappearance follow decision 3. Discarded coverage is unknown or truncated rather than current absence, older immutable parts cannot resurrect removed provenance, and a fixed ordered-log replay reproduces components, coverage, validity, observations, removals, truncation and conflicts exactly after the same initial state. The current native OTAP practice of stamping transport at sample times is incompatible with this rule; it is recorded as an implementation defect, not as an alternative temporal contract, and is not repaired here. Queries and scale: typed role discovery and projected diff or history use the role schema, not the accidental contents of the existing opaque string. Absent, unknown, truncated and explicitly ambiguous are distinct states. No Source or provenance label is synthesised for info(), vector matching or ordinary series identity, and provenance-only discovery, diff and reverse reads open zero sample payloads. Source identity and role data do not become a global identity dimension in external systems by default. Horizontally scaled systems may reuse these semantics, fixtures and immutable encodings, not unverified runtime packages, and no distribution, replication, placement, global registry, cross-node transaction or Source RPC follows. No generic graph or Entity-event subsystem follows. Exact supplied key names and acquisition protocol require their own implementation review; the channel must be explicit, configured, trusted and non-identifying, and today's AppendV2Options, native OTAP sink and other routes provide no such channel.
decisions.limits: Decision 5 does not decide PR99 syntax or metadata promotion aliases (decision 6), exact HTTP/JSON encoding and cursors (decision 7), target_info or promotion coexistence and migration (decision 8), actual admission, cache or retention budgets (decision 9), or performance targets and representative inputs (decision 10). Decisions 6 to 10 remain open and are excluded here. The receiver role is excluded from this phase; if it is introduced later it is optional, local and configuration-only and never disambiguates producers. Attribution is per-Resource-component, not per-field; independently versioned per-field provenance would require a separate relation and review. Trust is fail-closed, a proxy must not overwrite a known producer, and no supplied-key naming or acquisition protocol is selected here. Provenance cannot repair a collapsed stream, split streams, merge Resources or authorise reconciliation. No implicit expiry is introduced and no generic lease or TTL subsystem is selected. No multi-owner Source relation, generic graph, Entity-event ingestion, distribution, replication, placement, global producer registry, cross-node metadata transaction or Source RPC is selected. Partial observations add evidence but cannot remove an omitted component; only an explicit clear or a complete authoritative record within its declared scope changes the set. Current-phase limit: the incumbent stores one opaque SourceOwner string, and native OTAP emits the single owner 'otap' with content 'transport=otap' for every series at sample timestamps, with no producer, sender, typed components, coverage scope, completeness, ambiguity marker or trusted channel; every other route supplies no provenance record. The accepted roles, components, completeness and trust semantics remain explicit non-passing target cases, and the sample-time stamping is recorded as a separate defect.
